client.title: FileConfig
client.description:
The Aperio client configuration file (`aperio.yaml` or `~/.aperio.yaml`).

Layers, lowest first: built-in defaults, `~/.aperio.yaml`, `./aperio.yaml`
(or `--config`), the environment, the command line. A later layer wins,
key by key. Every scalar key has an environment variable, and a key nothing
reads is an error that names the key it was probably meant to be.

allow_server_forward.description:
Answer a `forward` check (`via: client`) whose endpoint the *server*
wrote, in its own visitor gate, rather than one of this client's
services. Such a check makes this client call a URL the server chose,
from this client's network, so it is refused unless this is set; the
checks this client's own `access:` declares are always answered.
Default: `false`.

bandwidth.description:
Total link capacity of this client: a budget divided across every
service and every parallel connection, so the sum the server is allowed
to push never exceeds it. Bit suffixes (`kbit`/`mbit`/`gbit`) count as
/8, byte suffixes (`kb`/`mb`/`gb`, or bare `k`/`m`/`g`) as x1000.

binds.description:
Tunnels `aperio-client bind` listens for on this machine, keyed by the
tunnel's name: a local port, or `{port, address, token, psk}`.

client_id.description:
This client's instance id, a UUID kept across restarts so failover can
recognize the process when it comes back. Unset, one is generated on
the first run and kept in `client_id_file`.

client_id_file.description:
Where a generated `client_id` is kept. Default: a file under
`~/.aperio/clients/` named after the config file this client reads, so
two projects on one machine never share an id and the file never lands
in a repository. A client with no config file, or one that cannot
write here, runs with a fresh id each time.

defaults.description:
What every service gets unless its own entry says otherwise: the same
keys a `services:` entry takes, apart from where its traffic comes from
and goes to. The environment and the command line write here too, so
`APERIO_TIMEOUT=60s` is `defaults.timeout`.

device_key.description:
Trust-on-first-use device key announced with the tunnel token, so a
server with token pinning on can bind that token to this machine.

device_key_file.description:
File holding the device key; a random one is generated and kept there
on the first run. Ignored when `device_key` is set directly. Default:
beside the kept `client_id`, under `~/.aperio/clients/`, for a client
that reads a config file; a client with none announces no key unless
one is given.

idle_timeout.description:
Shut this client down after it has served no request for this long
(unset = never). The scale-in half of `scaling`: the server never stops
anything, an idle client retires itself. The shutdown is graceful (the
server stops routing to it first, in-flight requests finish), and the
timer only starts once the client has served its first request, so a
slow cold start cannot make it exit before it is ever used.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

include.description:
Other config files to read before this one, each path relative to the
file that names it. Mappings merge key by key and anything else is
replaced, the same rule as every other layer: a fragment can add a
service, and this file wins over all of its includes. Later includes
win over earlier ones. Chains may nest up to five deep; a cycle is an
error.

log_format.description:
Log output format: `json`, or `pretty`/`text` for the human-readable
form. Unset auto-detects, a TTY gets `pretty` and a pipe gets `json`.

log_level.description: Log verbosity of this client (`RUST_LOG` overrides it). Default: `info`.

max_message_size.description: Largest single tunnel frame this client accepts. Default: `32MB`.

anyOf.description: A size: 512KB, 10MB or 1GB (binary units). A bare number is bytes.

messages.description: The local message faces, for an application on this machine.

name.description:
What to call this client on screen and in the server's logs, e.g.
`eu_server_1`. Lowercase letters, digits and `_`, like a service name.

A label, not an address: `client_id` stays the identity that failover
recognizes this process by, because that needs something unique and a
name is not. Unset shows the id.

otel_bridge.description:
Accept OpenTelemetry exports from things running next to this client and
carry them to the server, which forwards them to the collector it is
configured for. The point is an edge host that is allowed exactly one
outbound connection, the tunnel: no new firewall rule, no collector
credential at the edge. Applied at startup; a change needs a restart.

pid_file.description:
Path to write this process's pid to at startup, removed on a clean exit.
For an init system that wants one; a process supervisor usually knows the
pid without being told.

reload_drain.description:
How long in-flight requests may finish when a configuration reload
stops a service, before its tunnel connection is dropped. The client
announces `Draining` first, so the server sends it nothing new while it
finishes. `0s` drops the connection immediately. Default: `10s`.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

scaling.description:
Autoscaling: the endpoint the server calls when this client's services
need capacity. Applies to every service this client exposes; each
hostname bind gets its own record on the server.

serve_404.description:
Static-file services: HTML file served with status 404 for misses the
SPA fallback does not cover. Applies to every `serve:` directory of
this client.

serve_spa.description:
Static-file services: answer a navigation (`Accept: text/html`) that
matches no file with the root `index.html` and status 200, so a
client-side router owns its routes. A missing asset still 404s. Applies
to every `serve:` directory of this client. Default: `false`.

server.description:
The Aperio server to reach, the token to authenticate the tunnel with,
and how to get there.

services.description:
The backends this client exposes, keyed by name. Each opens its own
tunnel connection (or shares one, with `multiplex`).

subscribe.description:
Topic filters this client subscribes to, for messages from the other
clients of its organization. MQTT filter syntax: `+` is one level, `#`
is the rest. `$aperio/...` carries the server's own events.

An entry is a bare filter, or an object that also names a command to run
when a message arrives.

tunnels.description:
Private local services a peer client may reach with `aperio-client
bind`, keyed by the name binders use. Never exposed to the public web.

Access.description: `public`, one method block, or a list of them (any one admits).

anyOf.description: Anyone, with no login (needs a token that allows it).

AuthMethodSpec.description:
One entry of an `auth:` policy: which method gates the route, and the
settings that method needs.

`method` is deliberately a string here rather than an enum: an unknown one
should be refused by name, with the available methods listed, and a serde
"unknown variant" error inside an untagged enum says only that nothing
matched. The same reason `alert_rules` parses its `metric` by hand.

allowed_emails.description:
`sso`: the visitors let in, by the verified email the provider reports:
exact addresses, `*@domain`, or `*` for anyone the provider signs in.
One or a list.

audience.description: `jwt`: required `aud` claim, one or a list of accepted values.

cache.description:
`forward`: seconds to remember a verdict for an identical credential,
so a busy route does not pay a round trip per request. `0` asks every
time, and is the default when the endpoint is the server's own; over the
tunnel (`via: client`) the default is `30`, since the cold path there is
two round trips before the visitor's own request starts.

claims.description:
`jwt`: further claims a token must carry, each as an exact value the
claim must equal (`{groups: engineering}`).

client_id.description:
`sso`: the client id registered at the identity provider. Its redirect
URI is `https://<hostname>/aperio/sso/callback`, for each hostname the
gate covers.

client_secret.description: `sso`: the client secret registered with that id.

cookie.description:
`jwt`: read the token from this cookie instead of the `Authorization`
header, which is where an identity-aware proxy in front usually puts it
(Cloudflare Access writes `CF_Authorization`).

hmac_secret.description:
`jwt`: shared secret for HMAC-signed tokens (`HS256`), for an issuer
that is your own service rather than a provider with public keys.
Mutually exclusive with `jwks_url`.

issuer.description:
`jwt`: required `iss` claim. Strongly recommended: without it any issuer
whose key the JWKS happens to carry is accepted. `sso`: the identity
provider, whose discovery document names its endpoints.

jwks_url.description:
`jwt`: URL of the issuer's JWKS, the public keys its tokens are signed
with. Fetched and cached, and re-fetched when a token names a key id
that is not in the cache. Subject to the server's outbound policy.

method.description:
The gate: `none` (deliberately open), `basic` (a `user:password`
login), `bearer`, `jwt`, `forward`, `aperio` (this server's own
sign-in: a dashboard session reaching the hostname's organization, with
no credential to invent), or `sso` (a sign-in at an identity provider
of the visitor's, which grants nothing on Aperio itself).

query.description:
`bearer`: also accept the secret as `?aperio_token=`, for the callers
that cannot set a header. **Off by default**: a query string reaches the
access log, the `Referer` header, browser history and every proxy in
front, so this is a trade an operator makes on purpose.

request_headers.description:
`forward`: request headers copied to the subrequest.
Default: `cookie` and `authorization`, the two that carry an identity.

response_headers.description:
`forward`: headers of a `2xx` answer copied onto the request that goes
to the backend. This is how the pattern delivers an identity, and an
open list is how it becomes a header injection, so it is named
explicitly and empty by default.

scopes.description: `sso`: the scopes asked for. Default `openid email`.

secret.description:
`bearer`: the secret a caller presents as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`.
One or a list, all alternatives on the same gate, so a key can be
rotated by adding the new one before withdrawing the old.

timeout.description:
`forward`: seconds to wait for the endpoint. A timeout **refuses** the
request: an auth gate that opens when its check is unreachable is not a
gate. Default: `5`.

users.description:
`basic`: the credentials that open this gate, each `user:password`.
A single value or a list.

via.description:
`forward`: whose network the endpoint is dialed from. `server` (the
default) is the server's; `client` asks over the tunnel, and the client
serving the route calls its own internal endpoint, so `localhost:7070`
means the client's localhost. A policy written on a client must say
`client`, so the same word cannot mean two networks in two files.

BindEntry.description: Where and how to bind one named tunnel.

address.description:
Local address the listener binds; anything but the default puts a
deliberately unexposed service on the network and is warned about.
Default: `127.0.0.1`.

port.description:
Local port for this tunnel. Unset reuses the declared target's port when
it is free and unprivileged, and otherwise picks a stable port derived
from the tunnel's name (logged at startup).

psk.description:
Pre-shared key of an end-to-end encrypted tunnel; must match the `psk`
the declaring client wrote. Never sent to the server.

token.description:
Token to bind with, when the tunnel is reached with a different
credential than `server.token`.

BindValue.description:
One `binds:` entry, keyed by the tunnel's name (`pg_main`, or
`acme@pg_main` for another organization's).

A bare port number is the short form of `{port: <n>}`, since naming the
local port is the only thing most entries do.

anyOf.description: `pg_main: 15432`, the local port, everything else defaulted.
The full entry.

CircuitBreakerConfig.description:
Refusing to dial a backend that keeps failing. Answers 502 immediately
while open, so a dead backend stops being hammered and the visitor stops
waiting for a connection that will not come.

failures.description:
Consecutive failures that open the breaker. `0` disables it.
Default: the profile's, off unless `resilience` is `aggressive`.

open_for.description:
How long the breaker stays open before one request is let through to
test the backend again. Default: `30s`.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

max.description: Most connections the pool may grow to under load. Default: `min`.

min.description: Connections opened at startup and never dropped. Default: `1`.

Connections.description:
`connections:` as written in the file: a fixed count, or an elastic pool
with a floor and a ceiling.

A number opens exactly that many connections at startup and keeps them. A
range opens the floor and grows towards the ceiling under load. Unwritten,
a service on a connection of its own runs a small range, one to four: our
own measurements have a peak past which more connections cost more than
they return, and four is on the near side of it.

anyOf.description: `connections: 4`, opened at startup and kept.
`connections: {min: 1, max: 8}`, grown and shrunk with load.

Credentials.description: A `basic` method's credentials: one `user:password` or a list of them.

anyOf.description: A single `user:password`.
Several, any of which opens the gate.

HeaderDirectives.description:
Header edits applied to one direction of proxied traffic (request or
response): `add` sets headers (replacing any existing value of the same
name), `remove` strips headers by name (case-insensitive).

add.description: Headers to set, name → value; replaces an existing header of the same name.

HeaderRules.description:
Header add/remove rules for proxied HTTP traffic: `request` edits what the
local backend receives, `response` edits what the visitor receives.
Hop-by-hop and tunnel-critical headers stay managed by Aperio regardless.

request.description: Edits applied to forwarded requests before they reach the local backend.

response.description: Edits applied to backend responses before they return to the visitor.

HealthConfig.description:
Backend health probing for a service: the endpoint the client checks and
how patient it is before pulling the backend out of routing.

endpoint.description:
Endpoint to probe: a path like `/health` or a full URL. Unset = no probe,
and the service is routable as soon as the tunnel is up.

Against an `h2c://`/`h2://` target this names the **gRPC service** to
health-check instead: the probe calls `grpc.health.v1.Health/Check`,
because a plain GET cannot reach a server that speaks HTTP/2 with prior
knowledge and routes by method name. `/` asks about the server as a
whole, which is the usual answer. An absolute `http(s)://` URL still
means an ordinary HTTP probe, for a backend exposing health on a
separate port.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

threshold.description:
Failed probes in a row before the backend is reported unhealthy.
Default: `2`.

timeout.description:
How long to wait for each probe before counting it as failed.
Default: `5s`.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

wait_for_backend.description:
Hold the service out of routing until the backend first accepts a
connection, avoiding connection-refused errors while it boots
(superseded by `endpoint` when that is set). Default: `false`.

Hostnames.description:
A service's public hostname(s): one, or a list routing to the same
service. Each must be permitted by the client's token.

anyOf.description: A single hostname.
Several hostnames routing to the same service.

MessagesSection.description:
The local message faces: where an application on this machine can
publish and subscribe without speaking the tunnel protocol.

listen.description:
Local address the HTTP face listens on: subscribe with SSE, publish
with POST. Unset = no local listener.

OtelBridge.description:
The client's `otel_bridge:` block.

`PartialEq` so a config reload can notice that this block changed: the
bridge is the one facility a running client cannot rebuild, so the change
is reported rather than silently ignored.

listen.description:
Address for the OTLP/HTTP receiver, the one every SDK can reach with
`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`. Default: `127.0.0.1:4318`.

listen_grpc.description:
Address for the OTLP/gRPC receiver, for SDKs pinned to that transport.
Unset = no gRPC listener. Conventionally port 4317.

queue.description:
Exports to hold when the far end is not keeping up. Past this, the
newest is dropped and counted, never waited on: an exporter that cannot
hand off its batch blocks the application it is instrumenting, so
telemetry must never be the reason a tunnel stalls. Default: `256`.

transport.description:
How exports reach the server: `tunnel` sends them as frames on the
WebSocket this client already holds, `https` posts them to the server's
endpoint as ordinary requests. Default: `tunnel`.

`tunnel` is the one that keeps the "exactly one outbound connection"
property that makes this worth having; `https` exists because a client
whose telemetry is bursty may prefer it to stay off the tunnel entirely,
where it would share flow control with proxied traffic.

RetryConfig.description: Retrying a backend request that failed before any response arrived.

all_methods.description:
Retry non-idempotent methods (POST, PATCH) as well. Off by default,
because a retried write may reach the backend twice; the same reasoning
as the server's `resilience.failover.all_methods`. Default: `false`.

attempts.description:
Total attempts, including the first. `1` disables retrying.
Default: the profile's, `2` unless `resilience` says otherwise.

delay.description:
Wait before the second attempt, doubled before each further one.
Default: the profile's, `100ms` unless `resilience` is `aggressive`.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

ScalingDecl.description:
Autoscaling declaration: the URL the *server* calls when this service needs
capacity it does not have. Aperio never starts or stops anything itself, it
only signals a desired capacity to an endpoint the operator controls.

The record outlives the client process on purpose: the whole point of
`min: 0` is that the server can call this URL when nothing is running.

cold_start.description:
How long a visitor request may be held while a cold start completes
(`0s` = do not hold, answer immediately). Default: `45s`.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

cooldown.description:
Minimum gap between two calls for this bind. A new instance needs time
to appear; without this the server would ask again while it is still
starting. Default: `60s`.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

max.description:
Ceiling the server will never ask to exceed (0 = only cold starts, no
scale-out). Default: `0`.

min.description:
Instances that should always be running. `0` opts into scale-to-zero:
a request for an unserved hostname triggers a cold start instead of a
504. Default: `0`.

secret.description:
Sent as `Authorization: Bearer` on the outgoing call. Write-only: the
server never echoes it back and never logs it.

target_utilization.description:
Pool utilization above which the server asks for one more instance,
between 0 and 1. Default: `0.8`.

url.description:
Endpoint the server POSTs to when it wants more capacity. HTTPS only
unless the server allows plain HTTP; private and loopback addresses are
refused, since the caller is a lower-trust credential than an operator.

window.description:
How long utilization must stay above the target before scaling out.
Guards against reacting to a single spike. Default: `15s`.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

SecurityHeaderOptions.description:
Individually selected security response headers; only the set fields are
injected.

csp.description:
`Content-Security-Policy` value to inject (no default, CSP is
application-specific).

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

SecurityHeaders.description:
Security response-header preset: `true` enables the standard set (HSTS,
`X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`,
`Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`), a mapping picks
headers individually. Explicit `headers:` rules always win over the
preset.

anyOf.description:
`true` enables the standard preset, `false` disables it (e.g. for one
service when `defaults:` enables it).
Granular per-header selection.

ServerSection.description: The Aperio server this client connects to, and how it gets there.

api_key.description:
Admin API key used by `aperio-client api ...` calls, never by the tunnel
itself.

ip_family.description:
IP family used to dial the server: `auto` (tries both), `ipv4`, or
`ipv6`. Set `ipv4` when the server hostname resolves to an IPv6 address
this host cannot reach. Default: `auto`.

min_tls_version.description:
Lowest TLS version offered when dialing the server over `wss://`: `1.2`
or `1.3`. Unset leaves rustls' own set (1.2 and 1.3) in place, which is
the right default; pin it when a policy has to name the floor rather
than inherit it. A value this client cannot offer is refused at startup.

proxy.description:
HTTP proxy to dial the server through, for a network that allows no
direct outbound connection: `host:port`, or `http://host:port`, with an
optional `user:password@` in front. The client sends `CONNECT` and then
runs TLS inside the tunnel the proxy opens, so the proxy sees the
server's hostname and nothing else. Your own backends are never reached
through it. Unset: dial the server directly.

tls_cipher_suites.description:
Exact cipher suites offered when dialing the server, by their IANA
names, comma-separated. Unset leaves rustls' preference order alone,
which is almost always better. An unknown name is refused at startup.

token.description:
Tunnel token (master or a scoped dynamic token) that authorizes this
client.

url.description: URL of the Aperio server this client dials out to.

urls.description:
Further server URLs to fail over to, tried in order when `url` is
unreachable, for a redundant control plane.

ServiceCache.description:
The server-side response cache, as far as one service is concerned. The
server has to have `cache.enabled` for any of it to do something.

enabled.description:
Let the server cache this service's GET responses, per their
`Cache-Control`. Default: `false`.

offline.description:
Keep serving this service's cached responses (marked, even past their
lifetime) while no healthy client is connected, instead of failing with
504. Needs `enabled`. Default: `false`.

ServiceEntry.description:
One exposed backend. The key it is written under is its name: a-z, 0-9
and `_`, the handle the dashboard and the logs use. Every key of
`defaults:` is accepted here as well and wins over it.

access.description:
Who may reach the service: `public`, one method block, or a list of
them (any one admits). Unset, the server's own `access` decides, and a
site's `access` on the server wins over this either way.

allowed_ips.description:
Visitor IPs/CIDRs allowed to reach the service; unset = everyone.
Enforced by the server before dispatch.

bandwidth.description:
The service's share of the link: the server never pushes it faster
than this, and the share is split across its `connections`. Settled
against the top-level `bandwidth` budget when there is one. Bit
suffixes (`kbit`/`mbit`/`gbit`) count as /8, byte suffixes
(`kb`/`mb`/`gb`, or bare `k`/`m`/`g`) as x1000.

cache.description: The server-side response cache, for this service.

circuit_breaker.description: Refusing to dial a backend that keeps failing.

connect_timeout.description:
How long to wait for the TCP connection to the backend, separate from
`timeout`, which covers the whole request. A backend across a VPN needs
longer than one on loopback. Unset: only `timeout` applies.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

connections.description:
Parallel tunnel connections; the server's
`limits.connections_per_service` is the ceiling, announced on connect,
and a token may lower it further. The server load-balances across them
like separate clients, so a single dropped connection leaves no
visitor-facing gap. A number opens exactly that many at startup;
`{min: 1, max: 8}` opens the floor and grows towards the ceiling while
requests queue up, then shrinks back when they stop. Default:
`{min: 1, max: 4}` for a service on a connection of its own, and `1` for
one that shares a connection or whose bandwidth is paced, since the
rate is divided across the pool's ceiling. A connection the pool grew
that the server refuses as full stands down rather than waiting for room.

custom_name.description:
What to call the service on screen. Free text: any language, any
punctuation, spaces. Nothing addresses it, so nothing breaks when it
changes.

denied.description:
Redirect URL for visitors refused by `allowed_ips` when no other
client of the route admits them. Unset = stealth: the same answer as
an unclaimed route.

depends_on.description:
Services in this file that must have a live tunnel before this one
opens its own. Waits for them, then proceeds regardless after a bounded
grace period, because a dependency that never arrives must not keep a
service that could serve traffic off the air forever.

hostname.description:
Public hostname(s) that route to the service: one, or a list. Each must
be permitted by the client's token. `*` serves every hostname no other
service claims, and needs a token that is not limited to particular
hostnames. A service naming none is reached only by a hostname its token
grants, or a random subdomain the server hands out.

inspector.description:
Record this service's transactions for the server's request
inspector. Turning it off for a service that carries heavy traffic buys
back a mutex, two header clones and a capture entry per request, at the
cost of not being able to inspect or replay its requests afterwards.
Default: `true`.

metrics_labels.description:
Static Prometheus labels on the service's metric series, e.g.
`{env: prod, region: eu-west}`, so one Prometheus can serve several
environments without relabelling rules. At most 8 labels; names must be
`[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*` and the server drops anything else, including
the names it writes itself (`client_id`, `job`, `instance`, …).

min_tls_version.description:
Lowest TLS version accepted from an `https://` backend: `1.2` or `1.3`.
Default: rustls' own floor.

multiplex.description:
Carry the service on one WebSocket shared with the client's other
services, instead of a connection of its own.

What it saves is the whole cost of a connection per service: one
socket, one TLS session, one reader, one writer and one heartbeat. What
it costs is that the services then share a link, so a large response
occupies the writer the others send through, and a dropped connection
takes all of them down together. Two services are needed for it to do
anything, and `connections:` is not honored for a service that asks for
it, one connection is what multiplexing means. Default: shared, for one
of several services that writes nothing a shared socket would change (a
`connections:` above one, a `bandwidth:` of its own, `startup_delay:`,
`depends_on:` or `tcp_target:`); `false` keeps a connection of its own.

pass_hostname.description:
Forward the visitor's original Host header to the backend instead of
the target's. Default: `false`.

path.description: Public path prefix that routes to the service.

priority.description: Failover tier (0 = primary, higher numbers are standbys). Default: `0`.

resilience.description:
How hard this service works to answer when its backend fails: `off`,
`safe` (the default: an idempotent request that fails before any
response is tried once more) or `aggressive` (three attempts, and a
circuit breaker). `retry` and `circuit_breaker`, where written, win
over the profile's values.

response_timeout.description:
How long the server waits for this service to answer a dispatched
request before failing it: the service's own `gateway.response_timeout`,
for slow report and upload endpoints. Unset: the server's applies.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

retry.description: Retrying backend requests that fail before a response arrives.

security_headers.description:
Security response-header preset: `true` injects HSTS,
`X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and
`Referrer-Policy`; a mapping picks headers individually.

serve.description:
Serve a local directory of static files instead of forwarding to a
backend (instead of `target`); directories serve their `index.html`.

server_side.description:
Let the server reach `target` itself instead of relaying through this
client, when the server's `security.server_side_targets` permits that
address (needs a token that allows it). Saves the two hops a relayed
request makes, and is only useful when the target is somewhere the
server can already reach. Refused rather than ignored when the target
is not permitted, and cannot be combined with `serve:`, whose files are
on this machine. Default: `false`.

startup_delay.description:
Wait this long before the service opens its tunnel, for a backend
starting alongside the client that is not ready the moment the process
is. Default: `0s`.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

target.description:
Local backend to expose: a port (`3000`), a host, or a URL. `h2c://` /
`h2://` targets are dialed over HTTP/2 (gRPC backends, trailers
relayed); `unix://` targets forward over a Unix domain socket.

tcp_target.description: Raw TCP backend instead of HTTP (instead of `target`).

timeout.description:
How long to wait for the backend to answer before failing the request.
Default: `30s`.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

trim_bind.description:
Strip the `path` prefix before forwarding, so the backend sees `/` and
not the bind. Default: `true` when `path` is set.

webhook_inbox.description:
Persist inbound POST requests (third-party webhooks) into the server's
webhook inbox, for browsing and re-firing. Default: `false`.

ServiceLimits.description:
How much a service takes on: bodies, concurrency, redirects. The same
names as the server's own `limits`, at the scope of one service.

adaptive_concurrency.description:
Lower the announced `concurrent_requests` while requests queue up
waiting for a local permit, and climb back when they stop. The server
already queues rather than dispatching past the announced number, so
this is how a client that has become slow stops being sent work it
cannot do; the server then holds the request, picks another client, or
asks for capacity through autoscaling, all of which beat a refusal.
Needs `concurrent_requests`, since that is the number being moved.
Default: `false`.

concurrent_requests.description:
Most requests this service handles at once before the server queues the
rest. Unset: no limit of its own.

redirects.description:
How many backend redirects to follow transparently before passing one
through. Default: `5`.

request_body.description:
Largest request body visitors may upload to this service; the server
rejects bigger uploads with 413 before they enter the tunnel. Unset:
only the server's own `limits.request_body` applies.

anyOf.description: A size: 512KB, 10MB or 1GB (binary units). A bare number is bytes.

response_body.description: Largest response body this client relays to a visitor. Default: `50MB`.

anyOf.description: A size: 512KB, 10MB or 1GB (binary units). A bare number is bytes.

ServicePolicy.description:
What a service does with its traffic, as opposed to where the traffic
comes from and goes to. This is the shape of `defaults:`, and every
`services:` entry carries the same keys, so a value written once under
`defaults:` reaches every service that does not write its own.

access.description:
Who may reach the service: `public`, one method block, or a list of
them (any one admits). Unset, the server's own `access` decides, and a
site's `access` on the server wins over this either way.

allowed_ips.description:
Visitor IPs/CIDRs allowed to reach the service; unset = everyone.
Enforced by the server before dispatch.

cache.description: The server-side response cache, for this service.

circuit_breaker.description: Refusing to dial a backend that keeps failing.

connect_timeout.description:
How long to wait for the TCP connection to the backend, separate from
`timeout`, which covers the whole request. A backend across a VPN needs
longer than one on loopback. Unset: only `timeout` applies.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

connections.description:
Parallel tunnel connections; the server's
`limits.connections_per_service` is the ceiling, announced on connect,
and a token may lower it further. The server load-balances across them
like separate clients, so a single dropped connection leaves no
visitor-facing gap. A number opens exactly that many at startup;
`{min: 1, max: 8}` opens the floor and grows towards the ceiling while
requests queue up, then shrinks back when they stop. Default:
`{min: 1, max: 4}` for a service on a connection of its own, and `1` for
one that shares a connection or whose bandwidth is paced, since the
rate is divided across the pool's ceiling. A connection the pool grew
that the server refuses as full stands down rather than waiting for room.

denied.description:
Redirect URL for visitors refused by `allowed_ips` when no other
client of the route admits them. Unset = stealth: the same answer as
an unclaimed route.

inspector.description:
Record this service's transactions for the server's request
inspector. Turning it off for a service that carries heavy traffic buys
back a mutex, two header clones and a capture entry per request, at the
cost of not being able to inspect or replay its requests afterwards.
Default: `true`.

metrics_labels.description:
Static Prometheus labels on the service's metric series, e.g.
`{env: prod, region: eu-west}`, so one Prometheus can serve several
environments without relabelling rules. At most 8 labels; names must be
`[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*` and the server drops anything else, including
the names it writes itself (`client_id`, `job`, `instance`, …).

min_tls_version.description:
Lowest TLS version accepted from an `https://` backend: `1.2` or `1.3`.
Default: rustls' own floor.

multiplex.description:
Carry the service on one WebSocket shared with the client's other
services, instead of a connection of its own.

What it saves is the whole cost of a connection per service: one
socket, one TLS session, one reader, one writer and one heartbeat. What
it costs is that the services then share a link, so a large response
occupies the writer the others send through, and a dropped connection
takes all of them down together. Two services are needed for it to do
anything, and `connections:` is not honored for a service that asks for
it, one connection is what multiplexing means. Default: shared, for one
of several services that writes nothing a shared socket would change (a
`connections:` above one, a `bandwidth:` of its own, `startup_delay:`,
`depends_on:` or `tcp_target:`); `false` keeps a connection of its own.

pass_hostname.description:
Forward the visitor's original Host header to the backend instead of
the target's. Default: `false`.

priority.description: Failover tier (0 = primary, higher numbers are standbys). Default: `0`.

resilience.description:
How hard this service works to answer when its backend fails: `off`,
`safe` (the default: an idempotent request that fails before any
response is tried once more) or `aggressive` (three attempts, and a
circuit breaker). `retry` and `circuit_breaker`, where written, win
over the profile's values.

response_timeout.description:
How long the server waits for this service to answer a dispatched
request before failing it: the service's own `gateway.response_timeout`,
for slow report and upload endpoints. Unset: the server's applies.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

retry.description: Retrying backend requests that fail before a response arrives.

security_headers.description:
Security response-header preset: `true` injects HSTS,
`X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and
`Referrer-Policy`; a mapping picks headers individually.

server_side.description:
Let the server reach `target` itself instead of relaying through this
client, when the server's `security.server_side_targets` permits that
address (needs a token that allows it). Saves the two hops a relayed
request makes, and is only useful when the target is somewhere the
server can already reach. Refused rather than ignored when the target
is not permitted, and cannot be combined with `serve:`, whose files are
on this machine. Default: `false`.

startup_delay.description:
Wait this long before the service opens its tunnel, for a backend
starting alongside the client that is not ready the moment the process
is. Default: `0s`.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

timeout.description:
How long to wait for the backend to answer before failing the request.
Default: `30s`.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

trim_bind.description:
Strip the `path` prefix before forwarding, so the backend sees `/` and
not the bind. Default: `true` when `path` is set.

webhook_inbox.description:
Persist inbound POST requests (third-party webhooks) into the server's
webhook inbox, for browsing and re-firing. Default: `false`.

SubscribeEntry.description:
A subscription that may also run a command when a message arrives.

`run:` is a remote-execution primitive by design: a message from another
client of the organization causes a command to run here. Everything about
its shape follows from that. The payload never reaches the command line,
only stdin and the environment, so a message can never become part of the
command. Concurrency is capped and the run is timed, so a publisher in a
loop cannot fork a thousand processes or leave one wedged forever. And it
is per topic, opt-in, in a file the operator wrote.

env.description:
Extra environment variables for `run:`, on top of what the client sets.
The command inherits the client's own environment as well; this is for
the values that belong to *this* subscription. `APERIO_MESSAGE_TOPIC`
and `APERIO_MESSAGE_ID` are set after these and cannot be overridden,
since a command reading them must be able to trust what it finds.

max_concurrent.description:
Runs allowed at once for this subscription. Messages that
arrive while the cap is reached are dropped with a warning rather than
queued: a queue for a command that cannot keep up is the same problem
one step later. Default: `1`.

run.description:
Command to run for each message, through the shell. The message body
arrives on **stdin**, never as an argument; `APERIO_MESSAGE_TOPIC` and
`APERIO_MESSAGE_ID` are set in the environment. Unset = deliver only.

timeout.description:
How long a run may take before it is killed. A command that hangs must
not hold the subscription's one slot forever. Default: `60s`.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

topic.description: The topic filter to subscribe to.

SubscribeValue.description:
One `subscribe:` entry.

A bare filter is the short form: listen, and let whatever is attached to
the local face receive it. The object form is for a client that should
*act* on the message itself.

anyOf.description: `- deploy/web`, listen and deliver, nothing else.
The full entry, for a subscription that runs something.

TunnelEntry.description:
One `tunnels:` entry: a private local service (a database, SSH) a peer
client may reach with `aperio-client bind`, never exposed to the public
web. The key it is written under is its name.

custom_name.description:
What to call it on screen. Free text: any language, any punctuation,
spaces. Nothing addresses it, so nothing breaks when it changes.

encrypt.description:
End-to-end encrypt this tunnel between the two clients (X25519 +
ChaCha20-Poly1305); the server only relays ciphertext. TCP only.
Default: `false`.

idle_timeout.description:
UDP only: how long a relay may sit with no datagrams in either
direction before it expires; binders learn it via tunnel discovery.
Default: `60s`.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

protocol.description:
Transport of the tunnel: `tcp`, `udp` (best-effort datagram
relay), or `tcp/udp` for a service that is genuinely both (DNS, for
instance). A combined tunnel is one tunnel with one name and one local
port on the binder, answering on both transports. Default: `tcp`.

proxy_protocol.description:
Write a PROXY protocol v2 header to this backend before any payload
byte, announcing the visitor's real address. TCP only. Without it the
backend sees a connection from the client process and the visitor's
address is lost at the last hop. Turn it on only when the backend is
configured to expect the header (nginx `listen ... proxy_protocol`,
HAProxy `accept-proxy`, MySQL `proxy-protocol-networks`): a backend that
is not will read it as protocol garbage and drop the connection.
Default: `false`.

target.description: Local address this client dials when a peer binds the tunnel.

server.title: ServerSettings
server.description: Everything the server is configured with at runtime.

access.description:
Who may reach a proxied route when nothing more specific says: `deny`
(the default) refuses a route nothing declares, `public` serves it to
anyone, and a method block or a list of them gates it. A client's
`access:` speaks for its own service, and a site's `access` speaks for
its hostname over both.

advanced.description:
What the defaults are chosen for and almost nobody needs to touch:
per-stream flow control, and compressing tunnel frames.

audit.description: Rotation of the tamper-evident audit log.

cache.description: The server-side GET response cache for services that opt in.

dashboard.description: The built-in dashboard and its sign-in.

edge.description: Publishing the served hostnames to a dynamic edge proxy.

gateway.description: How long the server waits on a client.

identity_headers.description: Headers telling the backend who served and who visited.

limits.description: Ceilings that protect the server: body size, concurrency, tunnels.

oidc.description:
Signing in to the dashboard with an identity provider. It is the
operators' sign-in and gates no visitor by being configured; a route
that should ask for it says `access: {method: aperio}`, and visitors
sign in at a provider of their own with `{method: sso}`.

otel.description: OpenTelemetry trace export, and the bridge for clients' exports.

outbound.description:
Where the server may send callbacks it makes on its own initiative
(webhooks, autoscaling hooks, JWKS, OIDC, OTLP). Security-relevant.

proxy.description:
The reverse proxy or CDN in front of this server, and whose
`X-Forwarded-For` to believe. Security-relevant.

request_id.description: The request id sent to the backend and echoed to the visitor.

resilience.description:
How hard the server works to answer when a client fails: a profile,
`off`, `safe` (the default) or `aggressive`, and the failover and outlier
settings it stands for, each of which can be written to differ.

retention.description: How long recorded data is kept.

routing.description: How a request picks among the clients serving its route.

security.description: Fences around the server itself. Security-relevant.

sites.description:
What the server does for a hostname, or a path under one, by itself:
answers without a client, policy on proxied traffic, and what a
hostname says when nothing serves it. Each setting comes from the most
specific site that writes it; `hostname: "*"` is every hostname.

tls.description:
Serving HTTPS directly, with no proxy in front: certificates from files,
from an ACME authority, or both. Security-relevant, and read at start.

uptime.description: The availability history behind the dashboard's Uptime panel.

Access.description: `public`, one method block, or a list of them (any one admits).

anyOf.description: Anyone, with no login (needs a token that allows it).

directory.description:
The authority's ACME directory. Default Let's Encrypt; its staging
directory, `https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory`,
is the one to try a setup against without spending its rate limits.

email.description:
Where the authority sends notices about the certificates, such as one
about to expire that could not be renewed.

enabled.description:
Obtain and renew certificates automatically. Turning it on agrees to
the authority's subscriber agreement. Default `false`.

hostnames.description:
Hostnames to hold a certificate for from the start, such as the
dashboard's own. A wildcard needs a DNS-01 proof, which this server
does not make.

on_demand.description:
Also obtain a certificate the first time a hostname a client serves is
reached over HTTPS, holding that handshake until it is issued. Random
subdomains are left out: each would be a certificate of its own, and an
authority limits how many one domain may have. Default `true`.

Advanced.description:
What the defaults are chosen for and almost nobody needs to touch: how a
streamed response is paced, and how tunnel frames are encoded. Kept apart
so the settings an operator does decide are not read past these.

compression.description:
Offer per-message zlib compression to clients. Worth it on a slow or
metered link carrying text; it costs CPU on both ends. Default `false`.

stream.description: Per-stream flow control for streamed responses, WebSockets and TCP.

AlertRule.description:
One `alerts.rules` entry: a quantity the server measures, a bound, and how
long the condition must hold.

above.description: Fire while the value is strictly above this. Set this or `below`.

below.description: Fire while the value is strictly below this. Set this or `above`.

for.description:
Seconds the condition must hold before firing, and hold clear before
resolving. Default `0` = react on the first observation. Both directions
use it, so a value sitting on its threshold cannot alert every tick.

metric.description:
What to watch: `connected_clients`, `pending_requests`, `store_bytes`
(the SQLite store and its sidecars on disk), or `rss_bytes` (the server
process's resident memory, Linux only).

name.description:
Names the alert. It becomes the event's `kind`, which is what a webhook
receiver switches on, so it has to be unique.

client_down.description:
How long a known service may stay down before a `client_down` alert.
Unset = off.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

error_rate.description:
Failed-request fraction (`0.0` to `1.0`) that fires an `error_rate`
alert. Unset = off.

min_requests.description:
Requests the window must hold before the error rate may fire. Default
`20`.

rules.description: Operator-defined alerts over what the server measures.

window.description: Window the error rate is measured over. Default `5m`.

max_size.description: Rotate the audit log past this size; `0` = never. Default `10MB`.

AuthMethodSpec.description:
One entry of an `auth:` policy: which method gates the route, and the
settings that method needs.

`method` is deliberately a string here rather than an enum: an unknown one
should be refused by name, with the available methods listed, and a serde
"unknown variant" error inside an untagged enum says only that nothing
matched. The same reason `alert_rules` parses its `metric` by hand.

allowed_emails.description:
`sso`: the visitors let in, by the verified email the provider reports:
exact addresses, `*@domain`, or `*` for anyone the provider signs in.
One or a list.

audience.description: `jwt`: required `aud` claim, one or a list of accepted values.

cache.description:
`forward`: seconds to remember a verdict for an identical credential,
so a busy route does not pay a round trip per request. `0` asks every
time, and is the default when the endpoint is the server's own; over the
tunnel (`via: client`) the default is `30`, since the cold path there is
two round trips before the visitor's own request starts.

claims.description:
`jwt`: further claims a token must carry, each as an exact value the
claim must equal (`{groups: engineering}`).

client_id.description:
`sso`: the client id registered at the identity provider. Its redirect
URI is `https://<hostname>/aperio/sso/callback`, for each hostname the
gate covers.

client_secret.description: `sso`: the client secret registered with that id.

cookie.description:
`jwt`: read the token from this cookie instead of the `Authorization`
header, which is where an identity-aware proxy in front usually puts it
(Cloudflare Access writes `CF_Authorization`).

hmac_secret.description:
`jwt`: shared secret for HMAC-signed tokens (`HS256`), for an issuer
that is your own service rather than a provider with public keys.
Mutually exclusive with `jwks_url`.

issuer.description:
`jwt`: required `iss` claim. Strongly recommended: without it any issuer
whose key the JWKS happens to carry is accepted. `sso`: the identity
provider, whose discovery document names its endpoints.

jwks_url.description:
`jwt`: URL of the issuer's JWKS, the public keys its tokens are signed
with. Fetched and cached, and re-fetched when a token names a key id
that is not in the cache. Subject to the server's outbound policy.

method.description:
The gate: `none` (deliberately open), `basic` (a `user:password`
login), `bearer`, `jwt`, `forward`, `aperio` (this server's own
sign-in: a dashboard session reaching the hostname's organization, with
no credential to invent), or `sso` (a sign-in at an identity provider
of the visitor's, which grants nothing on Aperio itself).

query.description:
`bearer`: also accept the secret as `?aperio_token=`, for the callers
that cannot set a header. **Off by default**: a query string reaches the
access log, the `Referer` header, browser history and every proxy in
front, so this is a trade an operator makes on purpose.

request_headers.description:
`forward`: request headers copied to the subrequest.
Default: `cookie` and `authorization`, the two that carry an identity.

response_headers.description:
`forward`: headers of a `2xx` answer copied onto the request that goes
to the backend. This is how the pattern delivers an identity, and an
open list is how it becomes a header injection, so it is named
explicitly and empty by default.

scopes.description: `sso`: the scopes asked for. Default `openid email`.

secret.description:
`bearer`: the secret a caller presents as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`.
One or a list, all alternatives on the same gate, so a key can be
rotated by adding the new one before withdrawing the old.

timeout.description:
`forward`: seconds to wait for the endpoint. A timeout **refuses** the
request: an auth gate that opens when its check is unreachable is not a
gate. Default: `5`.

users.description:
`basic`: the credentials that open this gate, each `user:password`.
A single value or a list.

via.description:
`forward`: whose network the endpoint is dialed from. `server` (the
default) is the server's; `client` asks over the tunnel, and the client
serving the route calls its own internal endpoint, so `localhost:7070`
means the client's localhost. A policy written on a client must say
`client`, so the same word cannot mean two networks in two files.

dir.description: Directory the snapshots are written to. Required with `interval`.

interval.description: Time between snapshots. Unset = no backups.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

enabled.description: Turn the cache on for services that set `cache: true`. Default `false`.

max_stale.description:
How long past its lifetime a cached response may still answer while a
`resilience: true` service has no healthy client. Default `1h`.

negative_ttl.description:
How long an error or negative response (a `404`) is cached. `0s` =
never. Default `0s`.

size.description: Memory budget of the cache. Default `64MB`.

CertificateFiles.description: One certificate and its key, as files on the server.

cert.description: The certificate chain, PEM, leaf first.

Credentials.description: A `basic` method's credentials: one `user:password` or a list of them.

anyOf.description: A single `user:password`.
Several, any of which opens the gate.

enabled.description: Serve the dashboard. The API stays up either way. Default `true`.

fenced_login.description: Fence the sign-in to the hostname's organization. Default `false`.

hostname.description: A hostname whose root is the dashboard. One exact name.

ui_language.description:
Language the dashboard and the login page open in when the browser's
is not supported: en, de, es, fr, tr, ru, zh or ja. Default `en`.

cert_resolver.description: Traefik certificate resolver on the generated routers.

entrypoints.description: Traefik entry points on the generated routers.

include_offline.description:
Also publish hostnames a token permits but no client serves. Default
`false`.

service_url.description: This server as the edge reaches it, e.g. `http://aperio:8080`.

token.description:
Credential the edge proxy presents; setting it turns the
`/aperio/api/edge/*` endpoints on.

FailoverSettings.description: The failover a profile stands for, field by field.

all_methods.description:
Also fail over non-idempotent methods, which may then reach a backend
twice. `false` in every profile: it is a decision about the backend,
which no profile can make.

max_jumps.description: Re-dispatch attempts per request. `2`, or `3` when aggressive.

mode.description:
What to do when a client dies mid-request: `fail`, `retry`, `wait` or
`retry-wait`. `off`: `fail`; `safe`: `retry`; `aggressive`:
`retry-wait`.

anyOf.description: What to do when a client is lost while a request is in flight.

oneOf.description: Wait for the same client to reconnect.
Re-dispatch now, or wait for a candidate when there is none.

retry_on_5xx.description:
Re-dispatch a buffered response whose status is a retryable server
error to another client, sharing the jump budget. `true` only when
aggressive.

retry_statuses.description:
The statuses that count for `retry_on_5xx`; empty = every 5xx.
`[502, 503, 504]` when aggressive.

window.description:
Total time the waiting modes may spend across all jumps. `15s`, or
`30s` when aggressive.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

client_down_threshold.description:
Silence after which a client is dropped from routing (it rejoins on the
next heartbeat); four times this closes its connection. Default `15s`.

response_timeout.description:
How long a dispatched request waits for the client's answer. Default
`30s`.

timeout.description:
How long a request waits for a client to (re)connect before failing.
Default `10s`.

HeaderDirectives.description:
Header edits applied to one direction of proxied traffic (request or
response): `add` sets headers (replacing any existing value of the same
name), `remove` strips headers by name (case-insensitive).

add.description: Headers to set, name → value; replaces an existing header of the same name.

HeaderRules.description:
Header add/remove rules for proxied HTTP traffic: `request` edits what the
local backend receives, `response` edits what the visitor receives.
Hop-by-hop and tunnel-critical headers stay managed by Aperio regardless.

request.description: Edits applied to forwarded requests before they reach the local backend.

response.description: Edits applied to backend responses before they return to the visitor.

serving.description:
Tell the backend which client, organization and token served the
request (`x-aperio-client-id`, `x-aperio-org`, `x-aperio-token`).
Default `false`.

visitor.description:
Tell the backend who the visitor is (`x-aperio-visitor-how`,
`x-aperio-visitor-id`). Default `false`.

enabled.description: Record proxied transactions for the request inspector. Default `true`.

redact.description:
Mask credential headers and secret-looking body fields in the
inspector and its exports. Default `true`.

per_second.description: Requests per second the bucket refills by. Default `5`.

allow_http.description:
Allow a plain-http key-set URL in a client-declared gate. Default
`false`.

allow_private.description:
Allow a key-set URL resolving to a private or loopback address in a
client-declared gate. Default `false`.

concurrent_requests.description:
Proxied requests in flight across every tunnel; beyond it a request is
answered `429`. Default `100`.

connections_per_service.description:
Parallel connections one client may open for one service; a token may
lower it, never raise it. Default `16`.

ip_rate.description: The per-visitor-IP token bucket every request spends from.

request_body.description: Largest request body a visitor may send. Default `10MB`.

streams_per_ip.description:
Streamed responses one visitor address may hold open at once. `0` = no
limit. Default `0`.

tunnels.description:
Tunnel connections at once. A client holds one per connection it runs:
one for several services sharing it, which is their default, one per
service that does not, and a few more for a pool under load while there
is room. A reload briefly wants two. Default `64`.

websockets.description:
Proxied WebSockets open at once; beyond it an upgrade is answered `503`.
`0` = no cap. Default `10000`.

access_events.description:
Emit the per-request access event for successful requests (failures
always log). Default `true`.

access_log.description:
File the structured access log is appended to, one JSON line per
request.

sample_rate.description:
Fraction of successful requests that produce an access line, `0.0` to
`1.0`. Default `1.0`.

duration.description:
The first lockout's length; it doubles with each repeat, up to an
hour. Default `60s`.

threshold.description:
Consecutive failed sign-ins from one address before it is locked out.
Default `5`.

MaintenanceSchedule.description: One recurring maintenance window of a site.

days.description:
Weekdays the window runs on (`mon`..`sun`, long names accepted). Unset =
every day.

reason.description:
Shown on the maintenance page and in the dashboard while the window
runs.

to.description:
Local end time, `HH:MM`, exclusive. Earlier than `from` means the window
wraps past midnight, and `days` then names the day it *starts*.

tz.description:
IANA time zone the times are local to. Default `UTC`. A named zone
rather than a fixed offset keeps the window in place across a
daylight-saving change.

token.description:
Token required to scrape. Unset = a random one, generated once and
kept in the data directory.

allowed_emails.description: Who may sign in: exact addresses, `*@domain`, or `*`.

client_id.description: OAuth client id registered at the issuer.

default_grants.description:
What an email with no user record is granted at its first sign-in,
`<org>:<role>` entries. Empty = refused until granted.

groups_claim.description: The claim carrying the provider's groups. Default `groups`.

issuer.description: Issuer URL; setting it turns the dashboard's sign-on on.

redirect_url.description:
Fixed callback URL (`https://<host>/aperio/oidc/callback`). Set it:
derived from the request otherwise.

bridge.description:
Accept OTLP exports from tunnel clients and forward them to `endpoint`.
Default `false`.

enabled.description: Export a span per proxied request. Default `false`.

endpoint.description:
Collector base URL. Default `http://localhost:4318`, or
`http://localhost:4317` with `protocol: grpc`.

headers.description:
Extra headers on every OTLP request, where a collector's credential
goes.

protocol.description: `http` or `grpc`. Unset: port 4317 is grpc, anything else http.

sample_rate.description: Fraction of traces recorded, `0.0` to `1.0`. Default `1.0`.

allowlist.description:
Destinations (hosts, `*.suffix`, IPs or CIDRs) callbacks may reach;
empty = no restriction.

block_private.description:
With no allowlist, refuse destinations that are or resolve to internal
addresses. Default `false`.

no_proxy.description:
Destinations called directly rather than through `proxy`: names, or
`.suffix` / `*.suffix`.

proxy.description: HTTP proxy callbacks go through: `host:port` or `http://host:port`.

OutlierSettings.description: The outlier ejection a profile stands for, field by field.

eject_for.description: How long an ejected client stays out. `30s`, or `1m` when aggressive.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

enabled.description: Turn passive ejection on. `false` only when the profile is `off`.

max_failures.description:
Failures inside `window` that eject a client. `5`, or `3` when
aggressive.

window.description: Window the failures are counted over. `30s`.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

Pages.description:
A site's own answer pages, the HTML itself. The `*` site's are the
server's, used wherever no narrower site sets one.

maintenance.description:
HTML answered while a hostname is in maintenance (`503`). At most
512KB.

unavailable.description:
HTML answered when no client serves a route (`504`), instead of the
plain-text default. At most 512KB.

real_ip_header.description:
A header read before `X-Forwarded-For` for the visitor's address, such
as `CF-Connecting-IP` behind Cloudflare. Only with a trusted proxy.

trust.description:
Believe `X-Forwarded-For` from the direct peer. Turn on only behind a
proxy that overwrites it. Default `false`; implied by `trusted`.

trusted.description:
The proxies and CDN egress ranges in front of this server (IPs or
CIDRs). The visitor's address is found by walking `X-Forwarded-For`
back past these.

Redirect.description: A redirect: a site's own `redirect`, or its `fallback`.

permanent.description:
Answer `301` rather than `302`, which lets a browser remember it.
Default `false`.

preserve_path.description: Append the requested path and query to `url`. Default `false`.

url.description: Where to send the visitor, an absolute `http(s)` URL.

enabled.description:
Send the request id to the backend and echo it to the visitor. Default
`true`.

trust_inbound.description:
Adopt the visitor's own value when the request carries one. Default
`false`.

Resilience.description:
How hard the server works to answer when a client fails: a profile, and
the settings it stands for, each of which can be written to differ.

failover.description:
Re-dispatching a request whose client fails mid-flight. A field left
out is the profile's.

outlier.description:
Taking a client out of routing when it keeps failing, while its health
probe still reports green. A field left out is the profile's.

profile.description:
`off` (a failure is the answer, nothing is ejected), `safe` (the
default: an idempotent request is re-dispatched once to another client,
and a client that keeps failing is taken out of routing for a while) or
`aggressive` (more attempts, a retryable `5xx` re-dispatched too, a
waiting failover).

RespondRule.description: The fixed response of a site that answers by itself.

status.description: HTTP status to answer with. Default `200`.

access_log.description: How long access-log lines are kept.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

audit.description: How long audit events are kept; the hash chain stays verifiable.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

captures.description:
How long inspector captures and webhook inbox entries are kept. Unset =
kept, bounded only by their caps.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

db_max_size.description:
Cap on the database file; past it the oldest low-priority data is
pruned. Unset = unbounded.

anyOf.description: A size: 512KB, 10MB or 1GB (binary units). A bare number is bytes.

stats.description: How long day-granularity statistics are kept.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

alternate_servers.description:
Other Aperio servers (`ws://` / `wss://`) a client may fall back to,
announced on every handshake. At most 8.

lb_strategy.description: How a client is picked from the routed pool. Default `round-robin`.

oneOf.description: Prefer the lowest `priority` tier the clients announce.
Keep a visitor on one client with an affinity cookie.

preview_noindex.description:
Mark services reached through their random subdomain as not to be
indexed (`X-Robots-Tag` and a disallow-all `robots.txt`). Default
`false`.

random_subdomain.description:
Give every client a random hostname from this pattern, `*` being the
random label: `*.example.com` or `*-test.example.com`.

allow_http.description: Allow a plain-http autoscaling endpoint. Default `false`.

allow_private.description:
Allow an autoscaling endpoint on a private or loopback address. Default
`false`.

enabled.description: Honor the `scaling:` blocks clients announce. Default `false`.

record_ttl.description: How long a record nothing re-announces is kept. Default `30d`.

admin_allowed_ips.description:
Addresses (IPs or CIDRs) allowed to reach the dashboard and its API.
Empty = no restriction.

denied_ips.description: Addresses refused everything, checked before any other rule.

jwks.description: How far a client-declared `jwt` gate's key-set URL may reach.

login_lockout.description: Locking out an address after failed sign-ins.

secure_cookies.description:
Mark session cookies `Secure`. Unset, they are when `proxy.trust` or
`tls.enabled` is on.

server_side_targets.description:
Destinations (hosts, `*.suffix`, IPs or CIDRs) a client may ask this
server to reach itself with `server_side: true`. Empty permits nothing.

token_expiry_warning.description:
How long before a token expires the `token_expiring` event fires. `0s`
= never. Default `1d`.

token_pinning.description:
Pin a dynamic token to the first device key that presents it. Default
`false`.

ServerAccess.description: `deny` (the default), `public`, one method block, or a list of them (any one admits).

drain.description:
How long in-flight requests may finish before their connections are
ended, or `auto`. Default `0s`.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

timeout.description:
When shutdown stops waiting for anything still open and exits.
Default `10s`.

Site.description: One hostname, or a path under one, and what the server does for it.

access.description:
Who may reach this site: `public`, a method block, or a list of them,
the grammar a client's `access:` has. Written here it wins over what any
client serving the site declares, so the operator, not a tunnel, has the
last word on a hostname.

canary.description: Split the traffic between two versions of a service.

fallback.description:
Where to send visitors when no client serves this hostname, instead of
a `504`. A site with a `path` cannot have one: it is about the hostname.

headers.description:
Header edits on proxied traffic. Applied after the edits of every
broader site that matches, so `*` sets what every hostname gets and a
narrower site can override it.

hostname.description:
The hostname: exact (`app.example.com`), a pattern (`*.example.com`,
`*-pi.example.com`), or `*` for every hostname.

maintenance.description:
Recurring windows during which this hostname answers the maintenance
page by itself. A site with a `path` cannot have them.

pages.description:
This hostname's own `504` and `503` pages, over the ones a broader site
sets. A site with a `path` cannot have them.

path.description:
A path prefix under the hostname, on a segment boundary (`/api` covers
`/api/v1` but not `/apix`). Unset = the whole hostname.

rate_limit.description:
A ceiling on the requests per second this site takes from every visitor
together, beside the per-visitor limit.

redirect.description: Answer every request here with a redirect, without a client.

respond.description: Answer every request here with a fixed response, without a client.

timeout.description:
How long to wait for the serving client's answer, over
`gateway.response_timeout` and any `timeout` the client declared.

anyOf.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

waf.description:
Requests refused before they reach a client: `403` for a deny rule,
`413` for a `max_body` rule.

SiteCanary.description:
A site's `canary`: which service gets the new version's traffic, how much
of it, and how somebody opts in by hand.

Weighted routing and a header-based canary are the same mechanism seen from
two angles, which is why they are one block rather than two settings.

header.description:
Request header that sends this visitor to the canary whatever the weight
says, so a developer can reach the new version on demand.

service.description:
Name of the client service serving the new version. Clients announcing
this service name are the canary side; every other client serving the
site is the stable side.

value.description: Value that header must carry. Unset = any non-empty value.

weight.description:
Percentage of visitors sent there without asking, `0` to `100`. Default
`0`, which with a `header` set is the opt-in-only shape.

The split is decided per **visitor**, by hashing their address, not per
request: a per-request coin flip would send one page load's twenty assets
to both versions, which is a mixture rather than a canary and breaks the
thing being tested first. The cost is that the split is only as even as
the addresses are spread, so at low traffic or behind one large NAT
twenty percent may not look like twenty percent.

SiteRateLimit.description: A site's `rate_limit`: one token bucket shared by every visitor.

burst.description: Burst capacity. Default: the `rps` value, one second's worth.

methods.description:
HTTP methods the limit counts (unset = every method), so a write path
can be limited without throttling reads of it.

backlog_limit.description:
Backlog past which a stream whose client ignores the pause is dropped.
Default `16MB`.

min_throughput.description:
Bytes per second a stream's reader must take while data waits for it,
or the stream is ended. `0` = no floor. Default `0`.

pause_at.description:
Backlog of one stream at which its client is asked to pause. Default
`2MB`.

resume_at.description:
Backlog under which a paused client is asked to resume. Default
`512KB`.

acme.description:
Certificates obtained and renewed from an ACME authority, Let's
Encrypt unless another is named, proven with TLS-ALPN-01 on the HTTPS
port.

certificates.description:
Certificates you manage yourself, as PEM files. Each serves the names
written in it, a wildcard included, and is read again when its files
change, so a renewal by another tool needs no restart.

enabled.description:
Serve HTTPS on `port`, beside the plain listener on the boot `PORT`.
Needs certificates: `certificates`, `acme`, or both. Default `false`.

port.description:
Port of the HTTPS listener, on the boot `HOST`. An ACME authority
proves a hostname by connecting to it on 443, so with `acme` this is
443, or whatever forwards 443 to it. Default `443`.

redirect_http.description:
Answer plain HTTP with a redirect to HTTPS, except the health probes.
Tunnel clients then have to dial `wss://`. Default `false`.

WafHeaderMatch.description: A header condition inside a `waf` rule.

regex.description: Regular expression the header value must match for the rule to fire.

WafRule.description:
One `waf` rule of a site: a request is refused with `403` when every
condition it sets matches, or with `413` when it has a `max_body` and the
body is larger.

header.description: A header the request must carry, matching a pattern.

max_body.description:
Largest body the matched requests may carry, which makes this a `413`
size rule rather than a `403` deny rule.

anyOf.description: A size: 512KB, 10MB or 1GB (binary units). A bare number is bytes.

methods.description: HTTP methods the rule applies to (unset = any).

path.description:
Regular expression matched against the request path. It sees the whole
path, not the part under the site's `path`.

origin.description:
The public URL the dashboard is reached at; setting it turns passkeys
on. Its domain becomes the relying-party id.

rp_id.description:
A parent domain of the origin's host, so one passkey covers its
subdomains.

retry_schedule.description:
Waits between redelivery attempts after a failed delivery; empty = no
retries. Default `[1s, 5s, 25s, 1m]`.

items.description: A duration: 250ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d or 1w. A bare number is seconds.

expose.title: ExposeSpec
expose.description:
Desired state of a managed public listener. Runtime state is kept separate
so persisting a resource cannot falsely claim that a socket is listening.

advertised_host.description: Visitor-facing DNS name or IP. Does not alter bind, DNS or firewall configuration.

allowed_ips.description: Actual socket peers allowed to connect; empty permits every source.

org_id.description: Stable organization id, or `master`. Never `*` or a display name.

ExposeListener.description:
IPv6 listeners are explicitly v6-only. This removes platform-dependent
dual-stack overlap; IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses are rejected by validation.

IPv6 listeners are explicitly v6-only. This removes platform-dependent
dual-stack overlap; IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses are rejected by validation.
